result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers take the same clear position and fix double-assignments at the system level with server-side enforcement, inline conflict messages, and undo. A does better on keeping the fast path, with one-key presets, defaults carried over from recent jobs and shown next to each field, and keyboard-first focus. It also says plainly what to change and what to leave alone for each proposal. B is a bit shorter but less specific about defaults, and it keeps hover tooltips, which A rightly points out keyboard users never see. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers take the same position and fix double-assignment at the source with a backend block and inline warnings. B covers the fast path more concretely: one-key presets, remembered defaults shown with their assumptions, and keyboard-first entry that follows the order of the call. It also adds a named override, undo, and passive conflict badges. A is shorter and clear, but its fast-path details are thinner, while B is longer but still well organized.
